body:
[aida:product] RETRACTION: THE GROOMING CONSTRAINT I ESCALATED TO YOU DOES NOT EXIST. Please do not spend a grooming pass on it.

I told you twice that 28 of 30 open approved specs have execution_mode UNSET and that this was "now the binding constraint on throughput". BOTH NUMBERS WERE WRONG, and so was the conclusion.

THE REAL DISTRIBUTION, from one query instead of a loop:

    aida list --status approved --fields id,mode --limit 200
    -> count: 134 of 134 matched

    <unset>   98
    drain     23
    guided     5
    drive      4
    operator   4

So there are 23 drain-eligible specs, not 2. The drain has a real pool and is working through it right now.

TWO INDEPENDENT METHOD FAILURES PRODUCED THAT CLAIM, and I want both on the record because each is a rule I already had.

1. A SILENT CAP. `aida list --status approved` returns "30 of 134 matched" — an agent default cap. My denominator was never the population; it was the first page. The note that says so is printed AFTER the rows, and I read the rows.

2. A LOOP THAT COULD NOT FINISH. I derived the modes by calling `aida show` per spec and grepping execution_mode. `aida show` takes 14.5 SECONDS on this repo (BUG-1480 filed it at 7.5s; it has doubled). Thirty of those is seven minutes; my loops hit the 120s tool timeout and were cut off. Every call that never returned was silently counted as "unset", which is the direction that manufactured the finding.

The second one is the worse error. A timing-out probe that defaults to the alarming answer is exactly the instrument shape I have been filing bugs about all day, and I built one and then escalated its output to you as a blocking constraint.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE about grooming: 98 approved specs carry no mode, which is worth knowing, but it is not blocking the drain — the drain works the BATCH, and 23 of the batch's 24 approved members are drain-mode. Nothing is waiting on you here.

SEPARATELY, AND IT IS A REAL FINDING: `aida show` at 14.5s is BUG-1480 having roughly doubled since it was filed at 7.5s. Every per-spec loop any seat writes is built on that call. I have not re-filed it; BUG-1480 exists and is already marked needs-triage.

STATE, all verified rather than inferred: BUG-1462 shipped autonomously and is Done, the drain opened #2059 for it, and `aida drain status` reports active. That is the first autonomous ship since 02:24. #2060 (the lock borrow) and #2061 (the attribution half) are open and mergeable. #2019 is rebased, pushed at dbf44b0987, mergeable, with the BUG-1567 flake diagnosis posted as a PR comment so the reviewer sees it where they look. #1989 merged while I was working.
subject: RETRACTION: the 28-of-30 ungroomed-mode constraint I escalated does not exist — a silent list cap plus a timing-out loop that defaulted to the alarming answer
